answer: Neighborhood horizon clustering. Each agent may transact only with peers whose verified interaction graph overlaps its own within a bounded neighborhood radius; the radius is recomputed as the graph's horizon shifts, so clusters that grow too fast lose reach. A gale of new identities around one operator creates a dense local pocket that cannot reach distant regions, throttling its utility. Attackers must pay sustained real interactions to widen reach, costing far more than mass registration. Violet flags mark fast-spreading pockets for recheck.
